blocks.title: The short version
items: **Your writing is private by default.** Only you can read it, unless you make an entry public.
**It is encrypted, but not end to end.** Loore's server decrypts it to show it to you and to send it to AI. We don't read it.
**AI reads what you allow, and new entries allow it by default.** You can set any entry, or your whole account, to None.
**No ads, no tracking, no selling.** We never sell your data or use it for advertising.
**You can take your data and leave.** Export it, ask us for a copy, or delete it. A deleted account can be recovered for 30 days; after that it is deleted forever.

blocks.text: Loore is run by [OPERATOR NAME], [LEGAL FORM], company ID (IČO) [COMPANY ID], [ADDRESS], Czech Republic. We decide what happens to the personal data described here: we are its controller.
For anything about your data, write to [info@loore.org](mailto:info@loore.org). We answer within one month.

Your email address and username. If you sign in with X: your X user ID and handle. Your settings (such as your model, your privacy defaults and your time zone), when you accepted the Terms, and whether your account is approved. We need these to run your account.

Your entries, voice recordings and their transcripts, and the AI's replies. Earlier versions of what you edit. Drafts and thread names. What you save or import: bookmarks, clipped web pages, documents, tweets and conversations from other apps. And what Loore makes from it for you: your profile, intentions, todo list, AI preferences and other documents, and the audio when Loore reads text aloud. This is the service you use.
Embeddings: lists of numbers that describe the meaning of a text. We make them for every entry the AI may read and for every saved reference, so that you and the AI can search by meaning.

For each AI request: the model, the amount of text, the cost and the time. When you were last active and on which page. Which documents and references you opened, and what you said about Glean's picks. We use this to apply usage limits, to see what works and to fix what doesn't.
Feedback and answers to polls. We read them, with your username, because they are written to us. Bug reports and ideas you ask the AI to file go to GitHub (section 5).

If you subscribe: its level, its state and dates, whether you have used the trial and have ever paid, why a subscription ended (for example, a failed payment or a dispute), which reduced-price code you used, if any, and the reference numbers Stripe gives your customer record and subscription. Your card and billing details stay with Link and Stripe; we never see your card number.

Our server logs record each request: the address it came from (your IP address), your browser or app, the page or API path and the time. Some log lines also hold your email address, for example when we send you a sign-in link. Error reports go to Sentry (section 5). We use these for security and to fix faults.

items: **Our contract with you**, for running Loore: your account, your content, search, AI replies, usage limits and your subscription.

**Your consent**, where we ask for it: marking content for training, using both AI providers for background work, and seeding your Loore from your tweets. You can withdraw it at any time; that does not undo what happened before.
**Our legitimate interest**, for security, logs, error reports and statistics on use, and for the profiles we build for invited people before they join (section 7).
**Legal obligations**, for the records the law requires us to keep.

blocks.text: What you write and record is **encrypted at rest** with AES-256-GCM, with keys managed by Google Cloud KMS (envelope encryption). That includes your recordings, the audio Loore generates, your profile and your other documents. Sign-in links and access tokens are stored only as fingerprints (hashes).

items: entries you made public;
embeddings;
metadata, such as dates, privacy settings and which entry replies to which;
your email address, username and X handle;

a few short texts: the titles, links and authors of saved references, the titles and one-line descriptions of your documents, the headings of text read aloud, and the words the AI searched for while replying;
an X archive you are importing, for up to 24 hours, until you confirm the import.

blocks.text: Encryption at rest is **not end-to-end encryption**. Our server decrypts your content whenever it has to: to show it to you, to search it, and to send it to AI. The operator has access to the server and can technically decrypt your data. Our rule is that nobody reads users' content, not for debugging and not for experiments. We would only do it if the law required it, or if you asked us to. This rests on trust, not on cryptography.
Backups hold the data as it is stored: what is encrypted stays encrypted.
Loore works with two AI providers, OpenAI and Anthropic, through their APIs. You choose your model, and with it the provider for your replies. Some work always goes to OpenAI:

rows: The thread, the documents the AI may read (such as your profile) and what it finds in your entries
The provider of the model you use
Background work: your profile, intentions, recent context, todo list
Entries and documents the AI may read
Your model's provider, or both if you chose "Anthropic and OpenAI" under Background tasks
A nightly summary of your saved references
Your saved tweets, bookmarks and clipped pages
A draft answer to a poll, only if you ask for one
Your profile, recent context and intentions, or your recent writing the AI may read, as the poll says
The model the poll names when you ask, which can be the other provider
**The words you search for**, entries the AI may read, and saved references
OpenAI, **the words you search for also when your account is set to None**
The thread, your profile and intentions, and the day's public tweets from the Community Archive

Training, only for content marked Train

items: Nothing set to None is sent to AI, with one exception: the words you type into search go to OpenAI to search by meaning, also when your account is set to None.

Loore's apps offer recording only for entries the AI may read, because OpenAI turns every recording into text. A recording sent to Loore's API in another way is turned into text by OpenAI even if its entry is set to None.

Under OpenAI's and Anthropic's API terms, they don't train their models on what we send, except content you mark Train. Where we have a separate training key for a provider, content set to Chat is never sent with it.

With each request, OpenAI receives a code that stands for your account, so that it can act on one account's requests if its safety filter flags them. The code is not your name, email or account number, and nobody without our key can tell whose it is.
Background work often goes through the providers' batch services. Loore does not delete the files of a batch from OpenAI afterwards; how long OpenAI keeps them is set by OpenAI's terms.

rows: Everything Loore stores: our server, database, backups and encryption keys
Your email address and the emails we send you: sign-in links, confirmations and account notices. They contain nothing you wrote.

Error reports: where the code failed, the page or API path, your browser or app, sometimes your account number or email address. They are built to contain nothing you wrote. On every page load, the website also sends Sentry a short session record (that a session started, and whether it ended in an error). Your browser sends these directly, so Sentry sees your IP address.
If you subscribe: what you enter at checkout, such as your name, email, card and billing address. Link sells the subscription and handles that data under its own privacy policy.

If you sign in with X or connect it: X tells us your X user ID and handle, and with bookmark sync, your bookmarks, every night. We send X the IDs of saved tweets to check they are still public. We never post to X.

If you ask the AI to file a bug report or an idea, and confirm it: its title and text become a **public** issue in Loore's GitHub repository, labelled loore:<your username>. They stay public after you delete your account.
Your IP address and browser details, when a page loads Loore's fonts
Only if you open a saved YouTube video: the player loads from youtube-nocookie.com
The X handles and user IDs we look up. We download public tweets from it; we send it nothing you wrote.

blocks.text: We use no advertising, analytics or tracking services, and we never sell your data.

Our server is in the USA, and OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, X and GitHub are US companies, so your data leaves the EU. For each transfer we rely on a safeguard the GDPR allows: the EU–US Data Privacy Framework where the company is certified under it, or the European Commission's standard contractual clauses in the company's data processing terms.
7. Profiles we build before you join

We invite some people by hand. For some of them, before they sign up, we open a closed account under their X handle and fill it with their own public posts, from the Community Archive (a public archive of tweets) or from X's API. Loore's AI then drafts a private profile and intentions from those posts, with OpenAI and Anthropic models.

items: Nobody can see the account. It holds only posts that were already public. Posts fetched from X's API are also kept as files on our server, unencrypted, until the account's content is deleted.
We do this so that the person can start from their own words instead of a blank page. Our legal basis is our legitimate interest in that, weighed against theirs.
When you first sign in with X, Loore asks whether to seed your Loore from your public tweets. If you answer **Not now**, we import and build nothing more.
To remove what was already built, use **Delete all my content** on the Account page, or delete your account.
If you haven't signed up and want us to delete such an account, or not to build one, write to [info@loore.org](mailto:info@loore.org) with your X handle. We delete it.
We also keep our own copy of the Community Archive's public tweets, for this and for Glean.
**Private entries:** only you.

**Public entries:** every signed-in Loore member can open them. Once public sharing is on for your account, they are also on the open web: on your public page and in its feed, and a public reply also inside the thread it answers, on that thread's page. Our sitemap lists the public entries that start a thread. Search engines and other crawlers, AI companies' crawlers included, are allowed to read public pages. Public entries are stored unencrypted.

**Your username** appears with everything you make public. If you signed up by email, it starts as the part of your address before the @, without characters other than letters, digits and _, and with a number added if that name is taken. If you signed up with X, it is your X handle, and public entry pages carry your numeric X user ID in data meant for search engines. You can change your username on the Account page; links with the old name then lead to the new one, so the two names can be connected.
**Your account and content:** until you delete them.
**An entry you delete:** its text and recording are wiped 30 days later.
**Delete all my content:** you can restore it for 30 days; then it is deleted forever.
**Your account:** if you delete it, you can recover it within 30 days by signing in; after that it is deleted forever, with everything in it.

**Backups:** daily copies are kept for 28 days and server snapshots for 14 days, so what is deleted forever leaves the backups within another 30 days. A weekly copy kept outside Google follows the same limit.

**What stays after an account is deleted:** a record of what your AI use cost, without your name; an empty placeholder where other people replied under your entries; your username, reserved for a year so that nobody else can take it over; bug reports and ideas filed on GitHub through Loore, which stay public with the label loore:<your username>; if you used a reduced-price code, the record of that use with the subscription's Stripe reference number but without your account; and the reference numbers of the payment events Stripe sent us.
**A prefilled account nobody signed in to:** until we delete it, or until you ask us to.
**Server logs:** [LOG RETENTION].
**Error reports in Sentry:** 30 days.
**Purchases:** Link keeps the records the law requires for sales and tax.

**See and copy your data.** With craft mode on, **Export data** in the menu downloads the threads you started as a text file: your entries, the AI's replies, and documents pinned to them. It leaves out your replies in other people's threads, your saved references and documents not pinned to a thread. You can download each recording from its entry. For everything else we hold about you, write to us and we send you a copy.
**Correct it.** Edit or delete your entries, edit your profile, intentions and other documents, and change your username and email on the Account page.
**Delete it.** Delete single entries, all your content, or your account, as described in section 9.
**Take it with you.** Use the export, or ask us for a copy in a common format.
**Object, or ask us to restrict processing.** For example, object to a profile we built before you joined.

**Withdraw your consent** at any time: set content back from Train to Chat or None, or choose one provider for background tasks. To take back a yes to seeding your Loore from your tweets, write to us; there is no setting for it yet.
**Complain** to the Czech data protection authority, Úřad pro ochranu osobních údajů (ÚOOÚ), or to the authority in the country where you live.

blocks.text: To use any of these rights, write to [info@loore.org](mailto:info@loore.org) from your account's email address. We answer within one month.

items: Loore sets only the cookies that keep you signed in: a session cookie, and a cookie that keeps you signed in for 30 days. There are no advertising or analytics cookies, so we don't ask for cookie consent.
Your browser also keeps a few of your Loore settings, such as the theme, your last privacy and AI choice, and craft mode. They stay on your device; craft mode is also saved with your account.

The iPhone app keeps your sign-in in the phone's Keychain and its settings on the phone. While a recording uploads, its audio is kept on the phone; parts that failed to upload stay there, also after the app restarts, until they are sent. The app also keeps logs of its last 20 recordings, without audio or words, for diagnosing recording problems. It contains no analytics or tracking.
The Chrome clipper keeps its access token and the address and title of the last page you clipped in Chrome's storage for the extension.

blocks.text: Loore is for people aged 18 and older. If you believe someone younger uses Loore, write to us and we delete the account.
When we change this policy in a way that matters, we tell you in Loore. The date below shows the last change.
